assumptions: Canonical immutable Form field-name/order generation; expected Map operations hash disjoint lexical tokens, not full path prefixes.
ceilings: Normalized paths obey maxPathSegments and maxPathCodeUnits; name-index size is proportional to registered names.
deterministicWork: Proportional 250/500/1000-field/path batches stay below eight owner operations per field; metadata changes add no scans or insertions. Fifty paths at depths 128/256/512/1024 slice at most their total encoded code units; the deep-owner/root-owner witness performs at most depth + 100 probes.
contract.resourceRationale: A generation retains a token tree containing names and IDs, never prior states or field objects. Leaves allocate no child map. The first query scans existing chunks without allocating a retained index.
contract.proof: The first query scans existing chunks. The second builds a tree split at raw dot/bracket boundaries, retaining the separator on the following token and the first owner for duplicates. A query advances through non-overlapping tokens once, retains its longest owner, and stops at a missing edge or leaf. Metadata-only changes share the same cache; name/order changes invalidate it.
contract.adversarialWitness: Deep and shallow production queries are checked against the uncached external-state scan, including mutable external inputs. The 1024-segment fifty-path witness prevents repeated prefix hashing; DOM maps deep primary and related paths through this same export.

fullScan.rationale: At most one initial scan and one index construction per queried canonical name/order generation; external noncanonical states remain uncached to preserve mutable-input behavior.

contract.proof: Canonical Form state retains ID-to-index mapping and resolves one fixed-size chunk coordinate.
contract.adversarialWitness: First, middle, last, and absent IDs in a 10k-field canonical form perform one map lookup.

fullScan.rationale: Only forged external states use the compatibility-free validation boundary before becoming canonical.

variables.name: uSource
variables.meaning: fields owning issues from the requested source

variables.name: fField

variables.name: iIssue
variables.meaning: all retained form issues

contract.proof: The canonical source-owner delta set retains at most one current-owner cardinality of pending overlay entries; once cumulative effective changes exceed the current set size it compacts to the current set. Between compactions the retained base is therefore at most twice the current owner count and materialization replays at most one additional current-owner cardinality before emitting the explicit snapshot.
contract.adversarialWitness: Dense 10/100/1000-owner source replacement down to one owner compacts before enumeration, while regrowth to the full current owner set keeps replay work within three map entries per current owner.
deterministicWork: ISSUE-047 instruments production Map iteration after dense shrink and regrowth; query replay stays <= 3 * uSource and repeated enumeration never depends on the discarded historical owner cardinality.

fullScan.rationale: Canonical queries reuse the retained source-owner index; only forged input falls back to complete validation/projection.

fullScan.rationale: Canonical single-field updates use retained owner and relation indexes; only the explicit allIssues output scans retained issues.

contract.proof: The field-to-server-issue inverse index identifies removed issue IDs directly. Existing global by-ID membership determines global removal even when a defined primary field is unregistered. Only primary and related fields copy field chunks; changed global and allIssues snapshots are rebuilt coherently so later structural projection cannot resurrect removed issues.
contract.adversarialWitness: Changing one field in a 10k-field Form with one related server issue updates only associated field chunks and the one canonical issue output without scanning unrelated fields.

fullScan.rationale: The changed immutable allIssues array is an explicit full output snapshot; registered fields are not scanned.

variables.name: iInput

variables.name: iRemoved
variables.meaning: canonical issue records being replaced

contract.proof: Constructor preflight adds field/issue records and raw relation vector lengths before normalization. Canonical issue stores cache normalized record-plus-relation totals; mutations subtract removed records and reserve incoming lengths against the retained maxOutputNodes ceiling. No rejected relation vector is enumerated or copied.
contract.adversarialWitness: FRM-05 counts zero caller-element reads for over-budget relation vectors at 1, 10, 1000 and 250000 entries. Inclusive boundaries, cumulative insertion, replacement, reset, metadata and submit-failed keep the same private ceiling and preserve state on rejection.

fullScan.rationale: Only incoming record metadata and replaced canonical records are inspected; relation contents are validated only after reservation succeeds.

contract.proof: Retained source-owner and issue-relation indexes enumerate only affected fields; incoming and retained issues rebuild the explicit allIssues output once while changed field chunks are copied by ID.
contract.adversarialWitness: Replacing one source affecting two related fields in a 10k-field form rebuilds the issue output and copies only those field chunks without visiting the other 9,998 field records.

fullScan.rationale: Source-wide replacement is proportional to retained and incoming issues, affected relations, and bounded chunk paths; registered fields are not scanned.

contract.proof: Preflight reserves record counts and relation lengths before stable-ID normalization, projection and retained indexing. Each accepted layer visits bounded field/issue/relation input a constant number of times; canonical stores retain the output count and configured ceiling for later mutations.
contract.adversarialWitness: FRM-05 accepts inclusive record-plus-relation budgets and rejects an over-budget 250000-ID vector before reading any relation element; normal related issue projection and duplicate validation remain intact.

fullScan.rationale: External construction must validate and index every supplied field and issue exactly once per declared layer.

variables.name: oNode
variables.meaning: library-owned branch, wrapper, and output reference nodes

contract.proof: Construction validates each bounded entry and path once and allocates every output node once. Structural branches and repeated-leaf wrappers have separate ownership roles: wrappers remain leaves during collision checks and are frozen explicitly once, then structural branches are frozen with an iterative stack without traversing opaque caller values.
contract.adversarialWitness: A maximum-depth path and maximum entry set reaches every declared ceiling without recursive traversal or freezing caller-owned leaf containers.

fullScan.rationale: External construction must validate every supplied entry and freeze every library-owned output node exactly once.
